default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Expresses a habit or ongoing state (習慣を持っている: have/maintain a habit).
It seems that, appears to be (conjecture or judgment based on information or perception).
Japanese people love taking baths, and it seems that many people have the habit of soaking in hot water every day.
to enter, to get in, to take (a bath)
to have, to hold, to possess
When, at the time of (timing of an action or event: when catching a cold).
Whether or not (embeds a yes/no question into a sentence).
The fact that..., meaning that... (nominalizes a clause to explain the core issue).
Therefore, the question that arises is whether or not one should take a bath when catching a cold.
to enter, to get in, to take (a bath)
Advises what one should/should not do (やめたほうがいい: better to stop/should avoid taking a bath).
To become, change in state (弱くなっている: becoming weak/weakened).
What should I do? / What is best to do? (Used to ask for advice or guidance).
Of course, when you have a high fever, your body is weakened so it is better to avoid taking a bath, but what should you do when the fever has gone down considerably?
had better, should, would be better
what should one do, what to do
to be, to exist, to have
If (conditional form for hypothetical situations: if you have a fever).
Say that, believe that (used to quote an opinion or thought).
Think that..., believe that... (expresses the speaker's personal view or opinion).
In the past, it seems that many people believed that if you had even a slight fever, it was better not to take a bath, but I think taking a bath makes you feel refreshed and is good for you.
the past, former times, old days
even a little, even slightly, at all
if there is, if one has
had better, should, it is better to
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Indicates purpose (in order to do something: 'to show visitors...')
Indicates a scene or action currently taking place ('animals moving around')
Recently, in zoos, new display methods are being devised in order to show visitors animals moving around.
is being devised, is being considered
in order to, for the purpose of
Lists representative actions ('such as swimming, moving, flying')
Indicates a change of state to becoming able to do something ('have become able to...')
Expresses ability or possibility ('can observe, be able to see')
For example, at Zoo A, the animals are able to freely swim, move around, and fly, and we can watch them up close.
Indicates making an effort or arranging things so that something happens ('arranging so that visitors can enter')
Indicates that something also exists ('there are also such zoos')
In addition, to show animals that sleep during the day and wake up to become active at night, some zoos set special days to allow visitors in at night.
can enter, be able to enter
in order to, for the purpose of
Indicates a gradual change occurring from the past up to the present ('gradually changing')
In this way, zoos have been gradually changing in various ways.
are gradually changing, have been changing
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: Indicates the time an action takes place: "when / at the time of..." (short form verb + とき).
Indicates the ability to perform an action; here used in the past negative form できませんでした: "could not do...".
When I entered elementary school, I was unable to sit quietly in the classroom and listen to the teacher.
could not do, was unable to do
Expresses an action occurring before another action: "before..." (V-る + 前に).
To get used to / accustomed to doing something (V-ること + に慣れる).
Most of my friends attended kindergarten before entering elementary school and were used to listening quietly.
was used to, was accustomed to
To try doing something to see what it is like (V-て + みる).
Discovering an unexpected result or situation after doing something (V-たら).
Lists representative actions: "doing things like ... and ..." (V-たり V-たりする).
When I was four years old, I visited a kindergarten once and saw everyone singing the same song and dancing to the same music.
when (I) went and saw, after trying to go
To be interested / not interested in doing something (V-るの + に興味がない).
To decide on something (the content of the decision is marked by particle と).
Used at the end of a sentence to provide background information or explain a reason.
Since I was not interested in doing the same things together with everyone, I decided for myself not to go to kindergarten.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: Placed after a noun indicating the recipient of a letter or announcement ("To...")
Relative clause modifying a noun (people living in Sakura Garden)
To all residents living in Sakura Garden,
Polite honorific prefix attached before Sino-Japanese nouns to show respect
Particle を marks the object of the action (conducting the inspection)
Tomorrow, we will conduct an electrical safety inspection.
From... to... (indicating starting and ending points in time)
Modifying a noun (places where power is cut off)
There is/are... (indicates the existence of things or places)
From 10:30 AM to 12:00 PM, there will be locations where the power will be shut off.
to stop, to be cut off
to be, to exist, there is
Emphasizes the elevator as the main topic of the announcement
The elevator will not be operating.
does not run, will not operate
Placed at the end of a clause to indicate reason or cause ("because...")
Negative potential form, indicating inability to do something
Since power will also not be supplied to the 1st floor entrance door of the apartment building, it cannot be opened or closed.
During / throughout the period that an event or action takes place
Doing something in advance for preparation or to maintain a state
During the inspection, the door will be kept open.
Indicates cause or reason (because the room's electricity will not be cut off...)
Particle for non-exhaustive listing of nouns (TV, computer...)
Expresses ability or permission to do something
The room's electricity will not be shut off, so you can use the TV and computer.
will not stop, will not be cut off
can do, to be able to
Scheduled to / planning to do something
The room's electricity is scheduled to be checked on a different day.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Experiencing an event or occurrence (uses the particle を with the noun)
I experienced Japanese New Year for the first time.
Particle indicating a companion performing an action together (with someone)
Going to a certain place (particle に indicates destination)
On December 31, first, I went to a nearby supermarket with Mr. Nakayama at 9:00 AM.
first, first of all, to begin with
Pattern expressing a wish, blessing, or prayer (praying that..., hoping for...)
Quotation particle と used to directly quote the content of a prayer or thought
We finally managed to enter the shrine and prayed, "May it be a good year."
Set phrase: to draw a fortune slip
At the shrine, my senior drew a fortune slip.
Pattern used to explain or define the meaning of a concept (A means B)
Embedded indirect question pattern: whether or not...
Pattern expressing a state resulting from an intentional action (is written, has been done)
Drawing a fortune slip means receiving a piece of paper that indicates whether that year will be a good one or not.
Hearsay pattern used to convey information heard from others (heard that..., reportedly...)
I heard that good things were written on my senior's fortune slip.
The 〜てくる form indicates going somewhere and returning to the current location or home
And then, in the evening, we came back home.
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrasting/opposing meaning (but, however)
Nominalizes an action using 「の」: seeing someone doing something
I didn't buy anything, but I saw many people at the supermarket buying a lot more food than usual.
many people, crowd, large group of people
Dictionary form verb + ため: indicates purpose (in order to do something)
Plain form + そうだ: conveys hearsay or reported information (I heard that...)
I heard that it is to make special dishes eaten during the New Year.
New Year, New Year's Day, New Year holidays
purpose, in order to, for the sake of
Indicates the latest time limit by which an action must be completed (by / by the latest on...)
Indicates a range of time or space (from... to/until...)
Dictionary form verb + 習慣がある: to have the custom/habit of doing something
I heard that there is a custom of making that special food by December 31st and eating it continuously from January 1st to the 3rd.
to exist, there is, to have
make and, cook and, prepare and
Indirect quotation of what someone said previously (someone said that...)
Indicates the existence of people who perform an action (there are also people who...)
However, Mr. Nakayama said that nowadays there are also people who eat at restaurants starting January 1st.
to be, there are, exist (for animate things)
Going out towards a destination (particle へ indicates direction)
On January 1st, I went to a Shinto shrine with my senior and friends.
Emphasis and nominalization structure for a clause (The thing that... is that...)
Volitional form verb + とする: to intend to do, to attempt/try to do something
What surprised me was that there were so many people trying to go to the shrine, and they had been lining up for a long time.
trying to go, intending to go
was lined up, was waiting in line
Verb in ていた form + ら: expresses an unexpected discovery while an action was ongoing
Verb in て form + しまう: expresses an unfortunate or unintentional occurrence
Negative adjective form く + なる: transition of state to no longer...
While lining up outside the shrine, I suddenly couldn't find my wallet anymore.
was lined up, was waiting in line
not being found, unable to be found
Passive voice (盗まれる: to be stolen)
Time when another action occurs (when, while waiting)
Expresses an initial impression or assumption (thought that..., felt as if...)
Since I had heard that every year some people have their wallets stolen while waiting in front of the shrine, I thought mine had been stolen, but when I looked carefully, it was inside my bag.
to be stolen, to have something stolen
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: S City Art Museum is large.
From... to... (indicates a range of subjects, from children to the elderly)
Also, too (adds a similar item or circumstance)
Noun-modifying clause (modifies the following noun; かいた絵: painted pictures, かざった部屋: decorated room)
There are many rooms, and there are also rooms displaying paintings drawn by various people, from children to grandfathers and grandmothers.
to exist, to have, there is
to exist, to have, there is
Nominalizing a clause (the person who painted the pictures is...)
Passive voice (expresses an action performed on a subject; 選ばれた: was chosen)
Nothing but..., only... (nothing but great paintings)
The people who painted the pictures are residents of S City, and they are all fine paintings selected from among a great many.
Can do something (expresses ability: can view/look at)
Connects clauses to express cause or sequence (there are seats, so one can...)
There are also chairs in this room, so you can take your time viewing the paintings.
to exist, to have, there is
to see, to look at, to watch
can do, to be able to
Action is held/conducted (行われます is the polite passive form of 行う)
Concerts are also occasionally held in the spacious area on the first floor.
to be held, to take place
Emphatic structure: It is only when/that...
When doing something (when entering the room)
At this art museum, you only need to pay when entering the room with famous paintings.
to exist, to have, to be
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Passive voice (売られる), expressing that bananas are sold.
Expresses origin or an ongoing continuous state (coming from abroad).
Most of the yellow bananas sold in Japan come from abroad.
When, at the time of... (combined with noun + の).
Passive voice (取られる, 運ばれる) used to describe the action of harvesting and transporting bananas.
Used at the end of a sentence to provide an explanation or add explanatory context.
Bananas are harvested from trees while still green and transported to Japan.
Potential form in the negative (食べられません: cannot eat).
い-adjective (drop い) + くなる expresses a change of state (to become yellow).
Conjunction connecting two clauses with a contrasting meaning ('but').
Green bananas cannot be eaten as they are, but by the time they are displayed in stores, they have turned just the right yellow.
to line up, to be displayed
Expresses doing an action and returning (買ってきて: buy and bring back).
Expresses leaving something in a certain state (leaving the bananas as they are).
Natural/inevitable conditional: whenever the preceding action is taken, the following consequence naturally occurs.
If you buy yellow bananas from the store and leave them out, many small black spots will appear on them.
to leave as is, to set aside
い-adjective ending changed to く + なる expresses a change in quality (to become sweeter, more delicious).
Indicates that the result of a change is being maintained in the present state.
At that time, they have become sweeter and more delicious.
Doing something in advance or maintaining a state (putting it in the refrigerator and leaving it there).
Converts an い-adjective into a noun indicating degree (甘い -> 甘さ: sweetness).
If you keep them in the refrigerator, they will turn black, but the sweetness will not increase.
to put in and leave, to keep inside
to turn black, to become black
does not increase, will not increase
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: Indicates an action continuing uninterrupted ('to continue doing...')
My older brother often says, 'Living in a countryside place like this is no fun,' but I want to keep living forever in this town where I have many childhood friends.
to have, to exist, to be (animate)
all along, continuously, for a long time
want to continue living, want to keep living
this kind of, such, like this
the past, old times, long ago
Conditional form 'if... then...' (車があれば: if you have a car)
Used to list reasons or facts ('and also...', 'not only... but also...')
Nominalizes an action to serve as the subject ('walking is...')
It is a bit far to the station or hospital, but if you have a car it is no problem, and walking in a quiet place feels pleasant and is good for your health.
if there is, if you have
there is not, do not have
Modifies the following noun with a potential form verb ('a supermarket you can go to')
There is also a supermarket that you can go to by car.
can go, able to go (potential form of 行く)
Particle に used with transportation ('get on / ride a train')
Conditional form 'if... then...' (乗れば: if you ride/take the train)
Non-exhaustive listing of nouns ('such as... and...')
If you ride the train for two hours, you can go to places like department stores, movie theaters, and concert halls.
if you ride, if you take
and so on, etc., such as
Expresses a perspective or judgment from the speaker's standpoint ('for me...', 'to me...')
Indicates that something is easy to do or comfortable to experience ('easy to live in')
To me, this is a very livable town.
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: Expresses a state resulting from a deliberate prior action (transitive verb with てある).
There was a note left on Phong's desk.
Indicates the origin or person initiating communication ('from someone').
There was a phone call for you from Mr. Ueda of Company A.
Expresses that something was supposed to happen according to a plan or intention, but the actual outcome was contrary.
Masu-stem verb with そうにない expressing negative conjecture: 'hardly likely to...', 'doesn't seem possible to...'.
I was supposed to visit at 2:00 PM today, but the train has stopped and it looks like I won't make it in time.
to visit, to call on (humble form of 行く/来る)
unlikely to make it in time, doesn't look like one will be on time
Embedded question pattern using a question word: "(I do not know) when / what time...".
Connects clauses to express a cause or reason objectively and politely ("because...").
Since I don't know when the train will start running again, I don't know what time I will be able to arrive.
to run, to move, to operate
Honorific prefix attached before nouns to express politeness and respect toward the other person (ご都合).
Verb suffix expressing the speaker's desire or wish ("want to do").
I would like to ask about your availability, so I will call again.
want to ask, would like to inquire
to call, make a phone call
Pattern used to politely relay a message or information from a third party.
That was the message they left.
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Nominalizes the preceding clause with の to emphasize the information in the following clause ("The thing/moment that... is...").
Pattern used for self-questioning or posing a question, expressing contemplation ("I wonder if... / could it be that...?").
When is it that people feel they have become an adult, I wonder?
Indicates the point in time when an action or event has taken place ("when/at the time...").
Uses the particle と to quote the content of an answer ("to answer that...").
My older sister answered that it was when her relationship with our parents changed.
Nominalizes a verb (V-る + のは) to serve as the subject of the sentence: "Doing V is...".
Particle indicating the means or condition of performing an action oneself (自分で: by oneself).
Making decisions by oneself is a difficult thing.
Combines V-てみる (to try doing) and 〜たら (when/after): "When/after trying to do V, finding out that...".
Follows a verb or noun to indicate a point in time: "When / At the time of...".
Used after nouns or clauses to list non-exhaustive examples: "such as, and so on".
When I asked other people, there were various answers, such as when graduating from high school or college, or when going to a restaurant alone.
when I tried asking, upon asking
Used to list representative actions or states: "doing things like... and...".
Follows the potential form to express a change in state over time: "to become able to do something".
Used to express the speaker's conjecture or opinion softly and indirectly: "isn't it that...? / could it be that...?".
Isn't it through having various experiences—such as parting with family and friends to enter a new world, or becoming able to do something on one's own—that people gradually become adults?
to gradually become, to grow into
entering, stepping into (and doing other things)
can do, to be able to do
Prohibitive pattern indicating that an action is not permitted ("must not do").
Pattern expressing obligation or necessity to perform an action ("must do / have to do").
Indicates that whenever the preceding action occurs, the subsequent action follows as a natural habit or consequence.
Whenever my older sister was scolded by our parents with things like "Don't do that" or "You must do it this way," she would always get irritated and say, "So annoying!" or "I already know!"
must not do, should not do
such as, and so on, etc.
to be warned, be scolded, be reprimanded
Expresses a transition to a new state or the development of a new habit (to come to... / to reach the point where...).
Ever since / after doing the action in the preceding clause.
Hearsay marker: "I heard that..." / "Apparently..." (relaying information heard from others).
However, she said that after she started living on her own, she came to understand the feelings of her parents, who had always scolded her.
to live, to lead a life
い-adjective ending changes to 〜く + なる to express a change in state or quality (to become...).
Quotes the statement or assessment of a third person (saying that...).
She says that since then, her relationship with her parents has improved.
The particle に marks the mode of transportation boarded or used with the verb 乗る.
The other day, I took a taxi by myself.
Verb ます-stem + そう expresses that something is on the verge of happening or at risk of occurring (almost... / about to...).
Placed at the end of a sentence to explain the cause or reason for the preceding statement (That is because...).
That was because I was about to be late for a work appointment.
likely to be late, almost late
Sentence pattern used to express doing something or experiencing an action for the very first time.
It was my first time riding one alone.
Noun + になる indicates a change of state (e.g., to become an adult).
Uses the quotation particle と to quote past thoughts or internal feelings ("thought that...").
And then, I thought to myself, "Ah, I've really grown up into an adult too."
right?, hey; sentence-ending particle expressing emotion or reflection
Comparative pattern indicating "more than..." or "compared to...".
Embedded question pattern meaning "whether or not..." (e.g., whether it is okay to ride or not).
Adds another reason or aspect ("it is also because...").
Until now, I didn't take taxis because they cost more than the train, but it was also because I couldn't decide for myself whether it was okay to take one.
until now, up to now, so far
did not ride, did not take
allowed to ride, okay to take
could not decide, was unable to decide
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Indicates that an action is completely finished, or done unintentionally/regrettably.
When you think "I want to buy it," do you end up buying it right away?
wanting to buy, to want to buy
do you end up buying, will you end up buying
Expresses the time when an action takes place: 'when / at the time of...'.
Embeds an indirect yes/no question into a larger sentence: 'whether or not...'.
Volitional form used to suggest or invite someone to do something together: 'let's...'.
When shopping, let's first think about whether we will really use it.
first of all, first, to begin with
Expresses a natural condition or inevitable consequence: 'whenever... / if... then...'.
Lists representative actions or states: 'sometimes... sometimes...' / 'doing things like... and...'.
Expresses that an occasion or situation sometimes happens: 'there are times when... / sometimes...'.
Especially if you end up buying something thinking "it's cheap," you might find that you already have something similar at home, or it might turn out to be something you never use.
Embeds a question into the main sentence: 'whether or not...'
Also, whether or not you have a place to put it at home is important.
Negative conditional pattern: 'if not... then (leads to a bad result)'.
Expresses taking an action without doing the preceding one: 'without doing A, does B'.
Expresses an inevitable outcome or situation: 'ends up resulting in...', 'it turns out that...'.
If you don't think carefully before buying, you will end up throwing it away without using it.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Indicates past experience of having done something; negative form 「〜たことがありません」 means 'have never done'.
I had hardly ever been to the hospital.
Expresses a situation contrary to normal expectation ('even though, although, despite').
Nominalizes a verb or clause (used in 「言っているのを聞いて」: hearing [them] say..., and 「行かなかったのが」: the fact of not going...).
Indicates a change into a new state ('to become worried').
However, when I heard my hospitalized friend say, 'My stomach had been hurting continuously since a year ago, yet not going to the hospital was a mistake,' I suddenly became very worried.
one year ago, a year ago
was bad, was wrong, was at fault
Indicates the time or occasion an event occurs ('when, at the time of').
Placed at the end of a sentence to state a reason or cause ('because...').
Because there are times when I also have a stomachache.
Expresses conjecture or possibility with uncertainty ('might, may, perhaps').
Expresses a state or sensation that begins to appear and gradually intensifies ('started to hurt').
Indicates that while or after continuing an action, another event occurs or is discovered.
And as I kept thinking every day, 'I might have the same illness,' my stomach started hurting again.
while thinking, as one keeps thinking
started to hurt, began to ache
To try doing something to see how it goes ('tried going to get checked').
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrasting meaning ('but, however').
Passive voice; here, 「言われました」 means 'was told / informed (by the doctor) that'.
So, I went to the hospital yesterday to get checked, but I was told that there was nothing wrong with me.
none, not exist, there is no
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: Indicates the sender, origin, or source ('from someone/somewhere').
This is an email from Mr./Ms. Nakata.
An is always free on Friday evenings.
Also, she does not eat fish.
do not eat, will not eat
Placed after the recipient's name at the beginning of a letter or email (meaning 'To... / Dear...').
Expresses the speaker's intention or plan (plan to do something)
I plan to have a class drinking party (party) next Friday evening.
to hold, to host, to do
If the timing does not work for you, please contact me by email.
if inconvenient, if it doesn't work (for one's schedule)
please contact, please get in touch
Doing an action in advance or preparation for the future
Someone does something as a favor for the speaker or their in-group
Wanting someone else to do something for oneself
Also, since Mr. Yamakawa will buy the food in advance for us, I heard he wants you to let him know if there is anything you cannot eat.
best regards, please, thank you in advance
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: When... (expresses the time an action takes place: when using the room).
Passive form combined with ている expresses the current state of an object (is written on the paper).
Precautions for using the rooms at the community center are written on the paper.
Honorific form (sonkeigo) of Group 3 verbs (利用する → 利用される) used to show respect toward guests or customers.
To / Dear... (commonly used at the beginning of notices or letters to indicate the recipient).
To everyone using the rooms at the community center,
Lists representative actions (such as eating and drinking).
Please do not do V (a polite negative request or reminder).
● Please do not eat or drink inside the room.
From... to... (indicates starting and ending points in time).
Can do V, be able to do V (expresses capability or permission).
● Regarding the air conditioner, cooling can be used from June to September, and heating from November to March.
Want to do V (expresses the speaker's or user's desire).
When / At the time of... (indicates the timing or condition of an event).
Please do... (a polite request or instruction).
If you wish to use it during any other month, please inform the reception desk.
other than that, besides that, except for that
please tell, please say, please notify
Polite/honorific prefix 'ご' added before Sino-Japanese (kango) nouns to show respect toward the guest's actions.
After doing V, once V is done... (indicates that the preceding action must be completed before carrying out the next).
● After you finish using the room, please tidy up the chairs and desks.
please tidy up, please clean up
When... / At the time of... (emphasizes the timing of an action).
Doing something in advance / Leaving something in a certain state in preparation for a future purpose (here: keeping the door open).
When leaving the room, please leave the door open.
please leave open, please keep open
Such as... / Like... (gives a representative example: such as a guitar).
In the case of... / If... (used to state a condition or specific situation in notices or regulations).
Please... (formal honorific pattern used to politely request or instruct someone: ご利用ください).
● In the case of singing or playing musical instruments such as guitars, please use the music room.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Doing the subsequent action without doing the preceding one (walking instead of taking the elevator/bus).
Making an effort or trying to make a habit of doing something (trying to walk).
Used to modify or define the noun that follows (people who...).
Because exercise is good for health, more and more people are making an effort to walk instead of taking elevators or buses.
Te-form of an i-adjective used to connect clauses and indicate cause/reason (because one is busy...).
Time to perform an action (time to exercise).
The reason is that they are too busy and have no time to exercise.
nonexistent, there is none, not having
Follows the te-form to indicate trying to do something (in context: try starting).
Expresses the speaker's intention, thoughts, or plans (thinking of..., planning to...).
I am also thinking of trying to start with walking from now on.
Do not have to, no need to (no need to go to a sports club)
Used to list reasons or causes (not only no need to go..., but also simple...)
I think it is a good idea because there is no need to go to a sports club, and it is easy even for people who do not like exercise very much, like me.
even without attending, even if one does not go
Same as... (the same company as me)
Expresses a daily habit or repeated routine (regularly walking)
Erika, who works at the same company as me, also walks often.
Indicates a change of state (become enjoyable/more fun)
I heard that..., reportedly... (hearsay; conveying information heard from others)
I heard that she didn't like exercise at first, but walking became enjoyable, and she also started running.
did not like, was not fond of
To be told by someone (passive form of 言う)
Try doing something (try taking a look / try going)
Upon doing action A, discovering or realizing situation B (e.g., when going there, finding that it was crowded...)
When Erika told me, "I've been running in the park lately and it feels great. Why don't you check it out once?", I went to that park on Sunday and was surprised to find so many people running.
Looks like..., seems... (judgment based on appearance: 楽しそう - looks like having fun)
Erika seemed to be having a lot of fun, as she also had friends running with her.
To participate in or enter an event, competition, or tournament
I heard that..., reportedly... (relaying secondhand information heard from others)
I heard that Erika will participate in a marathon race for the first time next month.
Only... (used with negative verb forms to emphasize limitation or scarcity: could only run slowly)
Even though, although (expresses contrast or contrary to expectation)
To become able to do something, to reach the point of doing (indicates a change in capability or habit)
She mentioned that although she used to only be able to run very slowly, she can now run a bit faster, so she wants to become able to run 10 km in 1 hour.
Even if..., even though... (even after becoming an adult / growing up)
It seems that..., appears to be... (judgment based on observation or personal impression)
